exclusion_rules.comment: Cab-Chassis is a frame rails only truck. It cannot be combined with any specific body type.
Contractor Truck is a specific body. It cannot be a Utility or Service truck.
A Flatbed Dump is distinct from a heavy duty Dump Truck.
A Pickup Truck comes with a factory bed. It cannot be a Cab-Chassis or have a service body.
Mechanics truck implies a crane + utility body. It supersedes generic utility.
Bucket Truck has an aerial boom with a basket. It is a distinct body type and cannot have other major body configurations.
Crane Truck has a lifting crane with a hook. It is distinct from other body types.
Utility Truck - Service Truck has a service body with compartments. It cannot have major body modifications.
Flatbed Truck is a distinct body type. It cannot be combined with Pickup Truck.
Box Truck - Straight Truck is a specific body configuration. It cannot be combined with Cargo Van, Dry Van, or Reefer.
Rollback Tow Truck is a specific tow truck type. It cannot be combined with Flatbed Truck.
Reefer/Refrigerated Truck has a cooling unit. It cannot be combined with Box Truck - Straight Truck.
Dry Van is a specific body type. It cannot be combined with Box Truck - Straight Truck.
Cargo Van is a distinct vehicle type. It cannot be combined with Box Truck - Straight Truck.
Pickup Truck is a factory-built vehicle with integrated bed. It cannot be combined with Car Carrier or Flatbed Truck.
Car Carrier is a specialized tow vehicle. It cannot be combined with Pickup Truck.
Tractor is a frame-only unit designed to pull trailers. It cannot be combined with most body types.
Emergency Vehicle is a general category. It should not be combined with specific emergency vehicle types.
Specialty Tank Truck is a specific tanker type. It should not be combined with generic Tanker Truck.
Rollback Tow Truck is a specific tow truck type with a flatbed. It cannot be combined with other tow truck types.
Wrecker Tow Truck is a specific tow truck type with a boom. It cannot be combined with other tow truck types.
Selfloader is a specific tow truck type with wheel-lift arms. It cannot be combined with other tow truck types.
Sling Truck is a specific tow truck type with chains. It cannot be combined with other tow truck types.
Car Carrier is a specialized multi-vehicle transporter. It cannot be combined with single-vehicle tow trucks.
Stake Bed (rigid fencing/railing), Landscape Truck (nets/cages), and Hauler (decorative deck with hitch) are mutually exclusive bed types.
Landscape Truck (nets/cages) cannot coexist with Stake Bed (fencing) or Hauler (deck with hitch) - mutually exclusive bed types.
Hauler (decorative deck with hitch) cannot coexist with Stake Bed (fencing) or Landscape Truck (nets/cages) - mutually exclusive bed types.

truck_overlaps.decision_rule: Look at the FRONT of the cargo box (above the truck cab). 1. If there is a cooling unit (a machine with fans/vents) attached, it is a 'Reefer/Refrigerated Truck'. 2. If the front of the box is flat/smooth with no machine, it is a 'Box Truck - Straight Truck'.

Look at the bed sides. 1. If you see solid metal CABINETS or COMPARTMENTS with handles, it is a 'Utility Truck - Service Truck'. 2. If the sides are open with thin removable SLATS/STAKES, it is a 'Contractor Truck'. Ignore the rack. Cabinets = Utility.

FOCUS ON BED SIDES. 1. If you see built-in metal tool CABINETS/COMPARTMENTS with doors/handles running along the bed, it is a 'Utility Truck - Service Truck'. 2. If the bed is a FLAT OPEN PLATFORM with NO side compartments (you can see the deck surface), it is a 'Flatbed Truck'.

CHECK FOR STAKE SIDES. 1. If the bed has thin removable STAKES/SLATS/RAILS forming low sides, it is a 'Contractor Truck'. 2. If the bed is a FLAT OPEN PLATFORM with NO side rails or only a simple headache rack, it is a 'Flatbed Truck'.

LOOK BEHIND THE CAB. 1. If you see BARE FRAME RAILS with NO bed/body installed (open chassis, exposed rails), it is a 'Cab-Chassis'. 2. If there is ANY installed FLAT OPEN PLATFORM/DECK (even minimal), it is a 'Flatbed Truck'.

SCAN FOR A CRANE. Look at the rear corners of the service body. 1. If you see a mounting base with a hydraulic boom or a small crane, it is a 'Mechanics Truck'. 2. If it is just tool cabinets with no crane structure, it is a 'Utility Truck - Service Truck'.

Look at the area behind the cab. 1. If you see bare black metal frame rails (exposed chassis), it is a 'Cab-Chassis'. 2. If the frame is covered by a decorative deck (usually diamond-plate) and has a heavy-duty Fifth Wheel or Gooseneck hitch installed, it is a 'Hauler'.

Look at the Cab. 1. If the driver has a sliding side door and can walk into the cargo area (like FedEx/UPS), it is a 'Stepvan'. 2. If the cab is separate (conventional doors) and detached from the box, it is a 'Box Truck - Straight Truck'.
Look at the tip of the boom. 1. If there is a BASKET/BUCKET for a person to stand in, it is a 'Bucket Truck - Boom Truck'. 2. If there is a HOOK for lifting materials, it is a 'Crane Truck'.

VISUAL WHEEL CHECK: 1. Look at the REAR wheels. Do you see a deep concave (dish) rim? 2. Look at the FRONT wheels. Do you see a large protruding hub extension? If yes to either, it is 'Dually'. If wheels look flat/standard, it is 'Pickup Truck'.

CHECK THE BED STRUCTURE. 1. **Pickup Truck**: Factory integrated bed with solid side walls and tailgate, wheel well bulges inside the bed, typical pickup proportions. 2. **Flatbed Truck**: Flat OPEN PLATFORM with NO solid side walls (you can see the bed surface from the side), often wider than the cab, may have a simple headache rack.

IMPORTANT: Flatbed Truck and Dually are NOT mutually exclusive - a Flatbed Truck CAN be a Dually! Your task is to determine if this Flatbed Truck ALSO has dual rear wheels. Look at the rear axle: Do you see TWO separate wheels/tires on EACH side (4 rear tires total)? Look for deep dish rims, dual wheel assembly, or wider rear fender flare. Answer 'Dually' if you see dual rear wheels, answer 'Flatbed Truck' ONLY if you are certain it has single rear wheels.

IMPORTANT: Flatbed Dump and Dually are NOT mutually exclusive - a Flatbed Dump CAN be a Dually! If you see a FLAT OPEN bed (NO side walls) with a CURVED BULKHEAD behind the cab AND dual rear wheels, output BOTH 'Flatbed Dump' AND 'Dually'. Do NOT convert to 'Dump Truck' just because it has dually wheels - Dump Truck requires SIDE WALLS. Flatbed Dump has NO side walls!
VISUAL WHEEL CHECK: Look at the rear axle. If you see two tires side-by-side (4 total rear) or deep dish rims, it is 'Dually'. If single tires, it is 'Cab-Chassis'.

CHECK FOR SIDE WALLS: 1. **Dump Truck**: Has FULL-HEIGHT side walls (solid metal walls equal to or taller than cab height). The bed forms a deep enclosed 'tub' with tall rigid sides. 2. **Flatbed Dump**: Has NO side walls at all. The bed is completely FLAT and OPEN on the sides like a flatbed, but has a distinctive curved/arched front bulkhead behind the cab. If you see ANY side walls, it is NOT a Flatbed Dump.

CHECK FOR CURVED FRONT BULKHEAD: Look behind the driver's cab at the front of the bed. 1. **Flatbed Truck**: NO curved/arched bulkhead. May have a simple headache rack (vertical bars) but NO curved steel structure bending forward over the cab. 2. **Flatbed Dump**: HAS a distinctive curved/arched front bulkhead behind the cab that often bends/arcs forward over the cab like a shed-like structure. This curved bulkhead is the KEY differentiator. BOTH have NO side walls - the bulkhead is the only difference.

COMPARE SIDE WALL HEIGHT TO CAB HEIGHT: Both have side walls and curved front bulkhead. The ONLY difference is wall height. 1. **Dump Truck**: Side walls are TALL - height is EQUAL to or GREATER than the cab/driver compartment height. The cargo box looks deep and fully enclosed. 2. **Landscape Truck**: Side walls are SHORT - height is clearly LESS than the cab height. The walls look low/shallow compared to the cab. RULE: If carrier box height >= cab height = Dump Truck. If carrier box height < cab height = Landscape Truck. Output BOTH 'Dump Truck' and 'Landscape Truck' categories for landscape trucks.

HIERARCHY RULE: 'Box Truck - Straight Truck' is ALWAYS the PRIMARY category for any truck with a rectangular cargo box. 'Cutaway Cube Van' is a SECONDARY modifier describing chassis type ONLY. 1. Output 'Box Truck - Straight Truck' FIRST as primary. 2. ONLY add 'Cutaway Cube Van' as second category IF you can clearly see a pass-through door/opening from cab to cargo box. 3. NEVER output 'Cutaway Cube Van' alone or as the primary category. 4. If pass-through is not visible, output ONLY 'Box Truck - Straight Truck'.

CHECK FOR SLEEPING COMPARTMENT: 1. **Tractor**: A heavy-duty truck designed to pull semi-trailers with no specific day-cab or sleeper designation. May have a basic cab or extended cab but no distinct sleeping compartment. 2. **Conventional Day Cab**: A conventional style tractor WITHOUT a sleeping compartment. If you see a conventional cab with NO sleeper extension, it is 'Conventional Day Cab'. If the cab style is unclear or it's a basic tractor unit, classify as 'Tractor'.

CHECK FOR MOBILE HOME MODIFICATIONS: 1. **Toter**: A conventional cab specifically modified for transporting mobile homes. Look for specialized hitches, extended wheelbase, or mobile home transport equipment. 2. **Tractor**: A standard heavy-duty truck for pulling semi-trailers. If you see mobile home transport modifications, it is 'Toter'. Otherwise, classify as 'Tractor'.

HIERARCHY RULE: 'Ambulance' is a SPECIFIC type of emergency vehicle. 1. If you see a medical emergency vehicle with medical equipment, stretcher, or ambulance markings, classify as 'Ambulance'. 2. Only use 'Emergency Vehicle' for general emergency response vehicles that are NOT specifically ambulances or fire trucks. 3. Do NOT use both categories - choose the most specific one.

HIERARCHY RULE: 'Fire Truck' is a SPECIFIC type of emergency vehicle. 1. If you see a firefighting vehicle with hoses, ladders, or fire department markings, classify as 'Fire Truck'. 2. Only use 'Emergency Vehicle' for general emergency response vehicles that are NOT specifically fire trucks or ambulances. 3. Do NOT use both categories - choose the most specific one.

CHECK THE DRILLING MECHANISM: 1. **Auger**: A truck with a large drilling auger/bit mounted on a boom, used for drilling holes in the ground. The auger is typically a large spiral bit. 2. **Digger Derrick**: A truck with a boom and a drilling/digging bit, typically used for utility work. The bit may be more specialized for utility pole installation. If the drilling mechanism is clearly a large spiral auger, classify as 'Auger'. If it's a utility-focused digger, classify as 'Digger Derrick'.

CHECK THE LIFTING MECHANISM: 1. **Lugger**: A roll-off truck that uses a lugger mechanism (typically a chain or cable system) to lift dumpsters. 2. **Roll Off Truck**: A general category for trucks that drop off and pick up dumpsters. If you can see a specific lugger mechanism (chain/cable system), classify as 'Lugger'. If the mechanism is unclear or it's a standard roll-off, classify as 'Roll Off Truck'.

CHECK THE LIFTING MECHANISM: 1. **Lugger**: Uses a lugger mechanism (chain/cable) to lift dumpsters. 2. **Hooklift Truck**: Uses a hook arm mechanism to lift containers. Look at the lifting mechanism - if you see a hook arm, it's 'Hooklift Truck'. If you see a chain/cable lugger system, it's 'Lugger'.

CHECK FOR BRUSHES AND VACUUMS: Both are very similar. 1. **Street Cleaner**: A truck used to clean streets, usually characterized by large brushes and vacuums underneath. 2. **Sweeper**: A truck with brushes underneath for sweeping surfaces and gutters. They are essentially the same - if you see street cleaning equipment with brushes/vacuums, either category is acceptable. Prefer 'Street Cleaner' for municipal street cleaning vehicles.

CHECK FOR BED TYPE: 1. **Rollback Tow Truck**: Has a LARGE FLAT RECTANGULAR BED that tilts backward like a ramp. The bed covers most of the truck body. Vehicle sits fully on the flatbed. 2. **Wrecker Tow Truck**: Has a LARGE BOOM ARM OR CRANE mounted behind the cab. No flatbed platform - just a boom with winch cables/hooks. If you see a flat platform bed → Rollback. If you see a boom/crane → Wrecker.

CHECK THE LIFTING MECHANISM: 1. **Selfloader**: Has HYDRAULIC WHEEL-LIFT ARMS at the rear that grab the vehicle's wheels. Compact mechanism, no large boom. 2. **Wrecker Tow Truck**: Has a LARGE BOOM ARM OR CRANE with winch cables/hooks. Much larger mechanism than wheel-lift arms. If you see wheel-lift arms → Selfloader. If you see a large boom/crane → Wrecker.

CHECK THE LIFTING METHOD: 1. **Selfloader**: Uses HYDRAULIC WHEEL-LIFT ARMS that grab the vehicle's wheels automatically. Modern mechanism, no chains visible. 2. **Sling Truck**: Uses CHAINS AND HOOKS attached to a boom. Older style, chains/hooks are visible. If you see wheel-lift arms → Selfloader. If you see chains/hooks → Sling Truck.

COUNT THE VEHICLES: 1. **Rollback Tow Truck**: Carries ONE vehicle on a flat platform bed. The bed tilts backward like a ramp. Single vehicle fully on the flatbed. 2. **Car Carrier**: Carries MULTIPLE vehicles on racks/levels. Two or more levels of vehicle racks. Long trailer structure with multiple vehicle positions. If you see ONE vehicle on a flatbed → Rollback. If you see MULTIPLE vehicles on racks → Car Carrier.

CHECK THE BASE VEHICLE: 1. **Hauler**: A generic transport truck (can be semi-truck, medium-duty, etc.) pulling a trailer. Not specifically a pickup truck. 2. **Western Hauler**: A CUSTOM PICKUP TRUCK with an extended hauler bed. Has pickup truck cab and body style. Custom hauler bed with side storage boxes. Gooseneck hitch in middle of bed. If it's a PICKUP TRUCK with custom hauler bed → Western Hauler. If it's a regular truck pulling a trailer → Hauler.

CHECK THE TRANSPORT METHOD: 1. **Hauler**: A truck pulling a TRAILER with vehicles/cargo. Generic transport truck with trailer attachment. 2. **Car Carrier**: A specialized transporter with MULTIPLE VEHICLES ON RACKS/LEVELS. Two or more levels of vehicle racks. Long trailer structure designed specifically for multiple vehicles. If you see a truck pulling a generic trailer → Hauler. If you see multiple vehicles stacked on specialized racks → Car Carrier.

feature_checklist.prompt: Analyze the truck bed area specifically.

features.name: has_side_compartments
features.question: Are there built-in metal storage lockers or cabinets with handles on the sides of the bed?

features.name: has_removable_stakes
features.question: Are the sides made of thin removable slats or rails (wood or metal)?

feature_checklist.logic: 'Utility Truck - Service Truck' if features['has_side_compartments'] else 'Contractor Truck'
